name: batchnorm
summary: BatchNorm (NCHW 4D only). f16 inputs/outputs (x,y,gamma,beta), f32 stats (running_mean/var or save_mean/rstd, dgamma/dbeta). Forward supports inference(using running stats) and training(batch stats). Backward supports training+affine only. Correctness-first via atomic reductions.
contract: - gamma, beta: f16 when affine path
- inference affine:  inputs(5) = x, gamma, beta, running_mean, running_var ; outputs(1) = y
- inference noaff :  inputs(3) = x, running_mean, running_var             ; outputs(1) = y
- training  affine:  inputs(3) = x, gamma, beta                           ; outputs(3) = y, save_mean, save_rstd
- training  noaff :  inputs(1) = x                                        ; outputs(3) = y, save_mean, save_rstd
- training affine only: inputs(5) = x, dy, gamma, save_mean, save_rstd ; outputs(3) = dx, dgamma, dbeta
- training noaff: NotImplemented (even though supported() accepts it for dx-only, launch returns NotImplemented)
- Training stats: sum[c] = Σ x, sumsq[c] = Σ x^2 over N*H*W
- Forward output: y = ((x - mean)*rstd)*gamma + beta (gamma/beta optional, default 1/0)
- Inference uses running_mean/var, computes rstd = rsqrt(running_var+eps) inside apply kernel
abi: AttrBlob schema for forward: 'BNEP' (0x50454E42) = BatchNorm eps + flags.
- schema_id==0 or missing/short payload => eps=1e-5, use_running_stats=true
- If training signature is used (outputs==3), attr must NOT force running stats.
notes: Contiguity constraint is strict NCHW (strideW=1, strideH=W, strideC=H*W, strideN=C*H*W).
Correctness-first reduction: stats and bwd sums use atomicAdd into float[C]. This is simple but can be slow for large NHW/C due to contention.
Forward(training): save_mean buffer is reused as sum then overwritten to mean; save_rstd is reused as sumsq then overwritten to var then in-place to rstd.
Launch policy: threads=256, blocks=ceil(N*C*H*W / 256), blocks capped at 4096.
All heavy kernels use grid-stride loops over flattened total=N*C*H*W.
bn_finalize_mean_var uses 1D over C; then bn_var_to_rstd_inplace converts var->rstd in-place.

experiments.title: Replace atomic reductions with block/warp reductions
experiments.change: Compute per-channel sum/sumsq using hierarchical reduction (block partials -> final reduce) instead of atomicAdd into sum[C]/sumsq[C].
experiments.why: Atomic contention grows with NHW and hurts throughput; especially for large N*H*W and small C.
experiments.hypothesis: Reduce global atomic traffic; improve latency and effective bandwidth for training forward and backward sums.
experiments.proof: ncu: check atomic throughput, serialization stalls; compare kernel time vs baseline atomic version; validate correctness.
experiments.next: Try per-CTA shared partials + final kernel over partials; consider C-tiling when C large.

experiments.title: Fuse finalize + rstd + apply (training forward)
experiments.change: After computing sum/sumsq, fuse mean/var/rstd computation with apply using a single kernel over (C, NHW) with cached mean/rstd in registers or shared.
experiments.why: Currently 3 small C-kernels + 1 big apply kernel; extra launches and extra global reads of mean/rstd.
experiments.hypothesis: Fewer launches + fewer global reads => lower latency.
experiments.proof: nsys launch timeline + ncu memory reads; validate saved_mean/save_rstd outputs match reference.
experiments.next: If keeping save buffers, ensure they still end up with mean/rstd as required by backward.

measurements.notes: Report latency; optional: effective read/write GB/s for x/y and stat buffers; training forward has multiple kernels.
